Sanghasena Singh: "On the restauration of the Śrighanācārasaṃgraha", in: Philosophy, Grammar and Indology, Essays in Honour of Professor Gustav Roth, ed. H.S. Prasad, Delhi 1992, pp. 283-301]

body.translated_text: <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> (Compendium of the Conduct of <s>Śrīghana</s>)
First Chapter
Salutation to the <s>Buddha</s>

children.translated_text: Having bowed to him who has crossed beyond the ocean of the knowable, with all afflictions (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) eliminated,
The conduct of <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> (novice monks) shall be compiled. (1.1)

body.text: iti saṃghasenena saṃvihitoddhāre śrīghanācārasaṃgrahe buddhanamaskāro nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, 'Salutation to the <s>Buddha</s>,' in the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, as restored by <s>Saṃghasena</s>.
Second Chapter
The Status of the <s>Śrāmaṇera</s> (Novice)

children.text: śaraṇaṃ gatavān buddhaṃ dharmaṃ saṃghaṃ ca bhaktitaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s> with devotion,
Having taken the five training rules, who has gone forth following the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror), (2.1)
Who is restrained for life from killing, stealing, sexual intercourse, and false speech,
And from intoxicating drink, and from high and broad beds, (2.2)
And from accepting gold and silver — this one is considered a <s>śrāmaṇera</s> according to the Sage. (2.3)

body.translated_text: From dancing and the like, from garlands, perfumes, and the like, from eating at improper times,

body.text: iti saṃghasenena saṃvihitoddhāre śrīghanācārasaṃgrahe śrāmaṇerabhāvo nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, 'The Status of the <s>Śrāmaṇera</s>,' in the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>, as restored by <s>Saṃghasena</s>.
Third Chapter
The Means of [Maintaining] the <s>Śrāmaṇera</s> Status
1. The Training Rule of Abstaining from Killing Living Beings
Abandonment of Restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>)

children.translated_text: With the entire body or with any part of the body,
The renunciant (<s>yati</s>) shall not kill a living being endowed with the five limbs [i.e. five-branched]. (3.1.1)

children.text: mṛtyorvarṇa na bhāṣeta śastrahāraṃ na caiṣayet |
children.translated_text: One should not speak of the manner of death, nor procure a weapon;

children.text: vadhakena na cittena māraṇāya niyojayet || Śghs_3,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one, with murderous intent, commission [anyone] for killing. (3.1.2)
Purgatives, emetics, ointments, poisons, weapons, and preparations —

children.text: na kuryāt prāṇighātāya na ca garbhasya śātanaṃ || Śghs_3,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: One should not employ these for the killing of a living being, nor cause the destruction of a fetus. (3.1.3)
A vow-keeper should not perform prognostications based on dreams, owls' cries, and such omens;
Nor should [immoral conduct] be done for the sake of attaining the fruits of giving and morality. (3.1.4)
Whether in the middle, behind, or in front — wherever the murderous intent is directed,

children.text: [taṃ puruṣaṃ] dhnato hiṃsā nānyamityāha sarvavit || Śghs_3,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: The injury [falls on] that person [against whom intent is directed] — not another, says the Omniscient One. (3.1.5)
Deception, misleading, threats, <s>vetāla</s>-type sorcery and other preparations —
And poisoning — one should not perform these for the killing of embodied beings. (3.1.6)
Where on the road there is danger from thieves, snakes, armies, or the like,

children.text: tatpanthānaṃ na nāśāya dehināṃ kathayedyatiḥ || Śghs_3,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant should not reveal that path to cause the destruction of living beings. (3.1.7)
Where at a crossing there is danger from serpents and whirlpools,
[For the purpose of crossing a river,] one should not reveal that ford. (3.1.8)

children.text: kiñcid bhūpataye mā dāstvaṃ varaṃ jīvitaṃ tyaja |
children.translated_text: 'Do not give anything to the king; better to give up your life' —

children.text: iti baddhāyukte 'yuktaṃ vacanaṃ na vaded [yatiḥ] || Śghs_3,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: Such inappropriate words the renunciant should not speak to one who is bound. (3.1.9)
Where in a monastery there is danger from serpents, [wild beasts, or <s>yakṣas</s>],
One should not direct a visitor there with intent to cause harm. (3.1.10)

children.text: vyāghrādivyapadeśena śatruṃ hanyād hi yaḥ śaṭhaḥ |
children.translated_text: A deceitful person who would kill an enemy under the pretense of [warning about] a tiger and the like —
He should quickly be expelled from the monastery without readmission by the cell-dwellers. (3.1.11)
One should act such that not even one [being] perishes;

children.text: adharmyā na kriyā kāryā saṃsmṛtya krakacopamaṃ || Śghs_3,1.12 ||
children.translated_text: No unrighteous act should be done, remembering the simile of the saw. (3.1.12)
And as for <s>śrāmaṇeras</s> who have been employed as killers,

children.text: yugapat tatprayoge te nāśanīyā vihārataḥ || Śghs_3,1.13 ||
children.translated_text: Upon the simultaneous commission [of the act], they should be expelled from the monastery. (3.1.13)
The effort, the recognition [that the victim is] a human being, a man, the murderous intention,
And the destruction of life — these are the five components in the killing of a human being. (3.1.14)
If, through poison, weapons, and the like [provided] by a <s>śrāmaṇera</s>, intended for destruction,
A man dies by those very [means], then that [novice] loses his restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>). (3.1.15)
One who kills a human being unknowingly, through purchase or the like,
That renunciant incurs disturbance of restraint — [but this does not apply to] one who is insane or the like. (3.1.16)

body.translated_text: Misdeeds

children.translated_text: Bodily loving-kindness (<s>kāyamaitrī</s>) and the like should always be practiced by the renunciant toward beings;
Since the compassionate ones have said so, therefore one should not torment beings. (3.1.17)
One should not torment beings with bonds of wood, rope, or leather;
Nor should one compel them to enter water or fire, nor abandon them [to die]. (3.1.18)
Since wrong livelihood and the injury of worms, cattle, <s>ūpaka</s>-insects, and the like
Would result from plowing, therefore one should avoid that from afar. (3.1.19)
One should not brand a cow, buffalo, or the like, nor pierce its nose;

children.text: [yatiśca vividhān sattvān] vetrādinā na tāḍayet || Śghs_3,1.20 ||
children.translated_text: And the renunciant should not strike various beings with a cane or the like. (3.1.20)
Meat or a dish prepared specifically [for the renunciant] — if a renunciant were to eat it,

children.text: nighṛṇaṃ jāyate cittaṃ tasmāttannaiva bhakṣayet || Śghs_3,1.21 ||
children.translated_text: A merciless mind would arise; therefore one should never eat that. (3.1.21)
[Meat] is to be known by three modes: seen, heard, and suspected.

children.text: īkṣitaṃ yat svayaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ pratyāyitoditaṃ || Śghs_3,1.22 ||
children.translated_text: 'Seen' means witnessed by oneself; 'heard' means declared by a trustworthy person. (3.1.22)
From seeing the horns, feathers, and the like of deer and other [animals] confined in the house,

children.text: āśaṃkotpadyate [tatra] mamoddiśya hatā na vā || Śghs_3,1.23 ||
children.translated_text: A suspicion arises: 'Were these killed for my sake or not?' (3.1.23)
If the giver, when asked, says: 'These were killed on your account,'

children.text: tasmin gṛhe na bhuñjīta virataḥ prāṇināṃ vadhāt || Śghs_3,1.24 ||
children.translated_text: One should not eat in that house — [one must be] abstaining from the killing of living beings. (3.1.24)
Those [small creatures] killed by hawks and the like, and by eating rice, barley, and mung beans —

children.text: mātāpitrośca yajñasya kṛte doṣo 'sti nāśnatāṃ || Śghs_3,1.25 ||
children.translated_text: And for the sake of sacrifices to mother, father — there is no fault in eating [such food]. (3.1.25)
Meat, fish, and the like prepared for one <s>Śrīghana</s> (monk) specifically —

children.text: anyeṣāṃ śrāmaṇerāṇāṃ tadbhogāya na kalpate || Śghs_3,1.26 ||
children.translated_text: It is not suitable for the consumption of other <s>śrāmaṇeras</s>. (3.1.26)
Knowingly, one should not drink water from a river or the like that contains living creatures;
The beings considered [relevant] are the minute ones: mobile insects, worms, larvae, and the like. (3.1.27)
[For water purification,] one should maintain a water-strainer with a cloth filter;
For the purpose of avoiding destruction [of creatures], at least a case of fine cloth [should be used]. (3.1.28)
For one with divine sight and for the blind, the inspection of water is not required;
For one who can see the whirl at the tip of the thumb, it is not prohibited. (3.1.29)
'Lest there be an error of the eyes' — one should not examine it for too long;

children.text: kalpamātraṃ na vai kuryāt māyāśāṭhayasamanvitaḥ || Śghs_3,1.30 ||
children.translated_text: One should not do it for merely ritual purposes, being possessed of deception and fraud. (3.1.30)
The interval in which a sixty-year-old elephant turns around,

children.text: śakaṭaṃ vaṃśapūrṇaṃ vā sa kālaḥ salilekṣaṇe || Śghs_3,1.31 ||
children.translated_text: Or a cart full of bamboo [passes] — that is the [proper] duration for water inspection. (3.1.31)
Upper, lower, and middle — there are three levels of water;

children.text: yāyā bhūḥ śuddhimāyāti kāryaṃ kuryāttayā[yatiḥ] || Śghs_3,1.32 ||
children.translated_text: Whichever level is found to be pure, the renunciant should use that for his purposes. (3.1.32)
Where the large organisms sink to the bottom when struck by the palm of the hand,
[That] water should be taken [and] strained; if not [pure], through a five-finger [cloth strainer]. (3.1.33)
In water where living creatures adhere to the hand,
The renunciant should not wash his hands, feet, mouth, or clothes there. (3.1.34)

children.text: kule gatena praṣṭavyaṃ jalaṃ [hi] srāvitaṃ na vā |
children.translated_text: When going to a household, one should ask: 'Has the water been strained or not?'

children.text: neti cet saṃjñiko vācyaḥ srāvayetyitaro na tu || Śghs_3,1.35 ||
children.translated_text: If they say no, one who understands [signs] should tell [them] to strain it; but not the other [type of person]. (3.1.35)
However, if water containing creatures is placed in one's own vessel after straining,
One who has asked [about it] should release that [creature-laden portion] back to the same [source] himself. (3.1.36)
For seven days, or wherever drinking water remains [standing],

children.text: vihāre vā kaṭāhādau sthāpayet tadaśuṣyati || Śghs_3,1.37 ||
children.translated_text: In the monastery, one should store it in a basin or the like so it does not dry up. (3.1.37)
Or when the sky is raining, with clear water flowing abundantly,

children.text: nimnagānāṃ patiṃ pātaṃ gacchateti visarjayet || Śghs_3,1.38 ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant should release [the stored water with creatures] to flow down to the lord of rivers. (3.1.38)
With a small vessel whose mouth is bound with a pair of ropes to a very long stick,
The traveler should release the water below into [the larger body of] water. (3.1.39)

children.text: pariśuddhāścet peyaṃ jalaṃ tat srāvyamanyathā | Śghs_3,1.40 ||
children.translated_text: If they are pure, the water is drinkable; otherwise, it should be strained. (3.1.40)

body.translated_text: Having examined three small pots of water from the well on the road,

children.translated_text: Taking water with a rope-bucket is not approved when the water contains living creatures;

children.text: pibeti vaktuṃ dātuṃ vā na jātu kṣamate yatiḥ || Śghs_3,1.41 ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant should never allow himself to say 'drink' or to give [such water]. (3.1.41)
One should not announce loudly to others that a pond and the like contains creatures;
When asked 'what should I do?', one should reply to others: 'Do your task with discernment.' (3.1.42)
Even to the preceptor, one should say: 'Does this contain living creatures or not?' —
[Saying merely] 'the pond and so on' — such deception should not be practiced by the renunciant. (3.1.43)
Trees should not be watered with unpurified water;

children.text: upādhyāyādikasnānaṃ karttavyaṃ ca tathaiva na || Śghs_3,1.44 ||
children.translated_text: Nor should the bathing of the preceptor and others be done [with such water]. (3.1.44)
Buttermilk, <s>kāñjika</s> (fermented gruel), <s>sauvīra</s> (a type of vinegar), <s>maṇḍa</s> (scum), that struck with a stick, and the like —

children.text: na pibet na yatirdadyāt parasmai na bhuvi tyajet || Śghs_3,1.45 ||
children.translated_text: The renunciant should neither drink these, nor give them to another, nor discard them on the ground. (3.1.45)
Bedding that contains bedbugs should not be dried in the sun;

children.text: na hime kardame vā[pi] śītoṣṇavāriṇi kṣipet || Śghs_3,1.46 ||
children.translated_text: Nor [should it be placed] in frost or mud, nor thrown into cold or hot water. (3.1.46)
New construction should not be done with water containing creatures;
Having strained it until the end of the day, [the renunciant] should maintain the triangular cloth-strainer. (3.1.47)
The hired worker should be instructed thus: 'Do not [use the strainer improperly] — you, the triangular [cloth],

children.text: kapāt[tat] srāvayotkṣipya khallakaṃ ca vimocaya || Śghs_3,1.48 ||
children.translated_text: Lift from [the water], strain, and release the strainer [with its creatures back into the water].' (3.1.48)
Water should be strained through a triangular sevenfold [cloth]; that [should be done] with a <s>khallaka</s> (small water-pot).
[Then a counter-well should be made], or, having abandoned [that place], one should go to another region. [Śghs 3.1.49]
These [creatures], not having existed, come into being; having existed, they go to another state of existence.
At that time, new construction should be performed by one who follows the prescribed procedure. [Śghs 3.1.50]
From a bed-frame or the like, bound with fine cloth, [when a creature] rises [to a height of] four finger-breadths,

children.text: nadyādau jalamālokya kāryaṃ ca navakarmaṇi || Śghs_3,1.51 ||
children.translated_text: having observed water in a river or the like, [the procedure] should be performed during new construction. [Śghs 3.1.51]
A pair of sticks bound by a thread attached through two pierced holes [in the handles] —
the monk should place the straining vessel outside the <s>khallaka</s> (water-pot). [Śghs 3.1.52]
With a mind filled with compassion, sweet water containing living creatures
should not be released into alkaline water in the absence of emergency, by one who is mindful of purity. [Śghs 3.1.53]

body.translated_text: 2. The training rule on abstaining from taking what is not given
Loss of restraint (<s>saṃvara-tyāga</s>)

children.translated_text: That which is time-limited (<s>kālika</s>), watch-limited (<s>yāmika</s>), lifelong (<s>yāvajjīvika</s>), [provisions such as] ghee and the like;

that which should be worn (<s>pārihārya</s>), that which should not be deposited (<s>anādheya</s>), that which is allowable (<s>kalpya</s>), not allowable (<s>akalpya</s>), and undetermined (<s>akalpika</s>). [Śghs 3.2.1]
Earth, water, bipeds, quadrupeds, footless creatures, and trees —

children.text: tadgataṃ ca yatiḥ kiñcinnādadīta parasvakaṃ || Śghs_3,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: a monk should not take anything belonging to another that pertains to these. [Śghs 3.2.2]
Property [worth] a quarter of a <s>kārṣāpaṇa</s>, or half of that —
a monk who steals with thieving intent should be swiftly expelled by others. [Śghs 3.2.3]
When an elephant is seized from an enclosure, [the seizer becomes] a non-monk when [the elephant] has fallen [outside] on all four feet.
When [the elephant] has exited through a closed door, the monk indeed becomes a stealer of the elephant. [Śghs 3.2.4]
When a sugarcane stick fastened at the ankle is dragged far from the ground,
there is a breach of restraint when [it] is lifted up from the cage, like an elephant, for a <s>dvija</s> (twice-born). [Śghs 3.2.5]
One who carries [goods] from a region and transports message-related property,
[taking] from [one's own] body with a thieving mind, incurs damage to [his] restraint. [Śghs 3.2.6]
Having thought or heard 'He is dead' from a traveler or a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student),
a monk who, having given [something] to one staying at the boundary, [then] takes [it back], becomes a non-monk. [Śghs 3.2.7]
Whatever wealth belongs to a deceased <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice monk) or a perfected <s>Arhat</s>,

children.text: upādhyāyasya prāpnoti tadityevaṃ jagau muniḥ || Śghs_3,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: that falls to the preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>) — thus the sage declared. [Śghs 3.2.8]

children.text: hartturiṣṭāṃ diśaṃ yāyād vratī ced hastinaṃ haret |
children.translated_text: If a mendicant should steal an elephant, [the elephant] would go in the direction desired by the thief.

children.text: asau harttā vratī cauraḥ karipe hṛtasaṃjñini || Śghs_3,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: That taker, though a mendicant, is a thief, when the elephant has awareness of being taken. [Śghs 3.2.9]
By releasing both ends of a worship-robe or garland,

children.text: avanau taccyutau satyāṃ bhraśyate saṃvarād [yatiḥ] || Śghs_3,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: when those [ends] truly fall to the ground, a monk falls from [his] restraint. [Śghs 3.2.10]

body.translated_text: Having taken a pearl necklace or the like that was thrown [away] from a great family,

body.text: nyasya prasevikāyāṃ ca sahāyena ca hārayan || Śghs_3,2.11 ||
body.translated_text: and depositing it with a female attendant, and having a companion steal it — [Śghs 3.2.11]

children.translated_text: or, O child, if one takes by means of matted [hair], is he fallen from restraint?
Is it merely by [the object] falling from the foot, or by transgression of proper conduct? [Śghs 3.2.12]

children.text: rātrau gośakaṭāśvādīn kaścid vadhnāti ced yatiḥ |
children.translated_text: If a certain monk at night ties up cows, carts, horses, and the like [thinking],

children.text: etānete hariṣyanti tat kiṃ syāccyutasaṃvaraḥ || Śghs_3,2.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'These [thieves] will steal them' — would he then be one who has lost [his] restraint? [Śghs 3.2.13]

children.text: ṛjuke kīlake bandhe kaṭhine hāra[kaṃ] haran |
children.translated_text: One who steals a necklace from a straight, firm, hard fastening,

children.text: utkṣepaṇe ca cauraḥ syāt kuṭile śithile na tu || Śghs_3,2.14 ||
children.translated_text: and by lifting it, would be a thief; but not [if it is] from a crooked, loose [fastening]. [Śghs 3.2.14]

children.text: chidrayitvā ghaṭaṃ sarpiḥ kṣaudraṃ tailaṃ jalaṃ haran |
children.translated_text: A monk who, having pierced a pot, takes ghee, honey, oil, or water,
incurs disturbance of [his] restraint by the interruption of the contents. [Śghs 3.2.15]
When a house is being divided between two brothers, a monk who, desiring [to take] from the share of one,

children.text: bālamātraṃ bhūmiṃ yatiḥ syāt kṣatasaṃvaraḥ || Śghs_3,2.16 ||
children.translated_text: [takes even] the slightest [amount of] land, becomes one whose restraint is damaged. [Śghs 3.2.16]
One who, [having become] despairing of bowl and other [items] taken by a thief, takes [them] back again,
falls from [his] restraint; but the other [monk] does not incur a transgression. [Śghs 3.2.17]
If [something] were obtained through friendship, or given by cowherds and the like,
then no transgression is held for a monk who takes that. [Śghs 3.2.18]
[Only] a display of fear should be made for the recovery of bowl and robe;

children.text: rājani na vaded gatvaibhiścaurair muṣitā vayaṃ || Śghs_3,2.19 ||
children.translated_text: one should not go to the king and say, 'We have been robbed by these thieves.' [Śghs 3.2.19]
'You are expelling [what belongs to] the preceptors and teachers — that [property] of the two monasteries' —

children.text: tadityuktvā haredekaḥ syātāṃ dvāvapi taskarau || Śghs_3,2.20 ||
children.translated_text: having said 'that,' if one takes [it], both become thieves. [Śghs 3.2.20]
These two monks who steal their own property with a thieving mind —
one becomes a non-monk by [stealing] half a share, the other by [stealing] the expelled half. [Śghs 3.2.21]

children.text: dāsyāmaste samaṃ tiṣṭha dvāre kuryāma caurikāṃ |
children.translated_text: 'We will give [it] to you; just stand at the door; let us commit the theft' —
[if] one does what is thus proposed, a transgression [is incurred] together with the thieving accomplices. [Śghs 3.2.22]
When a visiting [monk], having stayed and departed, has forgotten [his] bowl and robe,

children.text: āgatya yo yatistacced gopayeccaura eva saḥ || Śghs_3,2.23 ||
children.translated_text: a monk who, coming [upon it], conceals that, is indeed a thief. [Śghs 3.2.23]
Thus all the resident [monks] become [ones] with damaged restraint.

children.text: sa eva yadi saṃsmṛtya nayatīha na kilviṣī || Śghs_3,2.24 ||
children.translated_text: But if that very [visiting monk], having remembered, comes and takes [it], there is no fault. [Śghs 3.2.24]
If a mendicant has another, with a thieving mind, bring the bowl of yet another,

children.text: ānāyayati sa tato doṣavān bhavati vratī || Śghs_3,2.25 ||
children.translated_text: he thereby becomes guilty. [Śghs 3.2.25]
'As long as worship [continues] for the sage, so too does [it continue] for the <s>saṃgha</s> (community)' —

children.text: iti yo 'nyasya datte sa bhavati kṣatasaṃvaraḥ || Śghs_3,2.26 ||
children.translated_text: one who, [thinking] thus, gives [the property] of another, becomes one with damaged restraint. [Śghs 3.2.26]
Having written, a deed of collection should be taken mutually from the <s>stūpa</s> and from the community.
And in the receipt of communal work, one should state this much; one who does otherwise commits [a transgression]. [Śghs 3.2.27]
One who takes [another's] own share as directed is a thief [and becomes a non-monk]; between those two,

children.text: dāsyāmīti ca viśvāsaṃ kṛtvā prāpnoti nāpadaṃ || Śghs_3,2.28 ||
children.translated_text: having made a promise saying 'I will give [it back],' one does not incur a transgression. [Śghs 3.2.28]

children.text: labhase tvaṃ labhe cāhaṃ yaṃ lābhaṃ tadāvayoḥ |
children.translated_text: 'You gain and I gain — whatever gain [arises], that belongs to both of us.'

children.text: iti lābhe samutpanne tato 'rdhena [sa] taskaraḥ || Śghs_3,2.29 ||
children.translated_text: When gain arises in this arrangement, by [taking] half, he becomes a thief. [Śghs 3.2.29]
Likewise in the case of gift-offering, between two rag-robe (<s>pāṃśukūlika</s>) [wearers],

children.text: bhinatti yaḥ kriyākāraṃ tataḥ sa cyutasaṃvaraḥ || Śghs_3,2.30 ||
children.translated_text: one who breaks the agreement thereby becomes one who has lost restraint. [Śghs 3.2.30]
[The community should distinguish] benefactors and malefactors [in distributing] food, drink, and other communal [property];
from <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) owners, kings, thieves, and the like, in due order. [Śghs 3.2.31]
Communal [provisions such as] morning meals and the like should be given even to <s>Śrīghanas</s>,

children.text: ālepanādi kurvanti vihāre yadi nānyathā || Śghs_3,2.32 ||
children.translated_text: if they perform plastering and the like in the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery) — not otherwise. [Śghs 3.2.32]
Having given to one standing at the boundary who serves the monks,
one should accept rice and the like by means of [sending] a boy [with] a <s>prastha</s> (measure). [Śghs 3.2.33]
One who has not abandoned hope should indeed reclaim [his] lost bowl and robe.
Thinking thus, a monk whose bowl and the like are lost should never abandon hope. [Śghs 3.2.34]
Those who, having taken up the purpose of study and learning, do not perform the practice of communal discipline,

children.text: kriyākāraṃ na kurvanti te jinoditalaṃghinaḥ || Śghs_3,2.35 ||
children.translated_text: are transgressors of the <s>Jina</s>'s (Conqueror's) teaching. [Śghs 3.2.35]
A banner or [its] sign should not be taken by a monk from a <s>stūpa</s>.
[However], if blown and dropped by the wind, it should be taken as a discarded rag-cloth (<s>pāṃśukūla</s>). [Śghs 3.2.36]

children.text: śulkakṛtyaṃ paradravyaṃ na nayet nāpi nāyayeta |
children.translated_text: A monk should not carry nor have [others] carry another's goods that are subject to customs duty.
A monk should not advise means for liberation from the payment of customs duty. [Śghs 3.2.37]

children.text: ratnaṃ datvā yatibhyaḥ prāk paścāt mārgayate vaṇik |
children.translated_text: If a merchant, having previously given gems to monks, later searches for them [saying],
'You are cheating [me]' — even so, that [gem] should be returned, having rebuked [the merchant]. [Śghs 3.2.38]
There is no customs duty on personal-use items of a sage, thus of mendicants.
One who engages in buying and selling should pay duty on other goods. [Śghs 3.2.39]
The rainy-season-retreat gain (<s>varṣāvāsika-lābha</s>) should indeed be given to one who has spent the rainy season.
[This applies] even to [cases involving] the destruction of life or celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>). [Śghs 3.2.40]
The request for the rainy-season retreat should be made by those who arrived earlier, first;

children.text: paścādupagataiḥ paścāt saṃghe yugapadeva ca || Śghs_3,2.41 ||
children.translated_text: by those who arrived later, later; and in the community, all at once. [Śghs 3.2.41]
One who, having abandoned monkhood out of disgust with material duties, again takes <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) —

children.text: bhikṣubhāvaṃ parityajya tasmai cāpyāha sarvavit || Śghs_3,2.42 ||
children.translated_text: regarding him too the Omniscient One (<s>Sarvavit</s>) has spoken. [Śghs 3.2.42]
Those who have not spent the rainy season, the confused, those of wrong views, the dead,
and those who have gone to another region — [these] five [types of] persons do not deserve [a share of] the gain. [Śghs 3.2.43]
When, after a gain has arisen, a monk dies [for whom it had been resolved] 'It should be given to that one,'

children.text: dātavyo niyataṃ tasmai sa vikalpitabhikṣave || Śghs_3,2.44 ||
children.translated_text: it should certainly be given to that designated monk (<s>vikalpita-bhikṣu</s>). [Śghs 3.2.44]
Even for one who has gone to another region, [the share] should be kept in the <s>kalpa-mandira</s> (designated hall).

children.text: traye kurvanti cānarthaṃ tebhyo deyaṃbudharna hi || Śghs_3,2.45 ||
children.translated_text: Three [of these types] cause harm; a wise one should indeed not give to them. [Śghs 3.2.45]
'I will give a covering, a robe, [or its] price' — through [meeting] four conditions,

children.text: āpnoti sammukhībhūtān lābho netareṣu ca || Śghs_3,2.46 ||
children.translated_text: one obtains gains [when] present; not in other [conditions]. [Śghs 3.2.46]
The rainy-season-retreat gain goes to one who has spent the rainy season.

children.text: tadetarasya doṣo na gṛhṇato dāyakecchayā || Śghs_3,2.47 ||
children.translated_text: There is no fault for the other who accepts at the donor's wish. [Śghs 3.2.47]
Time-limited (<s>kālika</s>), watch-limited (<s>yāmika</s>), lifelong (<s>yāvajjīvika</s>), weekly (<s>sāptāhika</s>);
dead [monks'] robes, minor requisites, regular, untimely, [and] robes —
gains [arising from] hut-establishment, birth, awakening celebrations, and great occasions —
tenfold gains reach those persons who are present. [Śghs 3.2.49]
[Property] not to be deposited (<s>anādheya</s>), [that is,] the preceptor's property, communal bedding and seating —

children.text: vikretavyaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ kṛtvā paudgalikaṃ na ca || Śghs_3,2.50 ||
children.translated_text: this should not be sold, nor should it be consumed having been made personal. [Śghs 3.2.50]
When a different item is given, the <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should redirect it to the appropriate place. (3.2.51)

body.translated_text: In the communal [property] that is present, [belonging] to the <s>Buddha</s> of the four directions —

children.text: tūṣṇīṃ datvā gate deyaṃ buddhe muktāphalādikaṃ |
children.translated_text: Having silently given [the item] and departed, one should offer things such as pearls to the awakened one;
To the community assembled from the four directions, [one should offer] bedding, seats, and cloth. (3.2.52)
A substantial item taken by another — the intention [to keep it] with that awareness constitutes the thought of theft;
Displacement from one's position, combined with the five factors — such a one ceases to be a <s>yati</s> (renunciant). (3.2.53)
Another restrained one who perceives what was given, what is one's own, or what was taken by another,

children.text: na tāvatkālikaṃ svāṃśād gṛhṇan jahāti saṃvaraṃ || Śghs_3,2.54 ||
children.translated_text: Does not lose his <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic restraint) by temporarily taking from his own share. (3.2.54)
Having taken what was not given and leaping up, going in the four directions,
And sitting down again in that very place — such a one has his <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic restraint) impaired. (3.2.55)
One who takes another's property through ignorance, such as something not purchased,
That <s>yati</s> (renunciant) incurs disturbance of <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint), but not if he is insane or the like. (3.2.56)

body.translated_text: 3. The training rule on abstinence from sexual intercourse
Abandonment of <s>saṃvara</s> (monastic restraint):

children.translated_text: Into the openings — anus, urinary passage, or mouth — of a man, woman, or <s>paṇḍaka</s> (eunuch), [inserting] the sexual organ,

children.text: kṣiptvā nigamayet svādaṃ sa [yatiḥ] kṣatasaṃvaraḥ || Śghs_3,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: If one completes the act with relish, that <s>yati</s> (renunciant) has his <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint) destroyed. (3.3.1)
Human and non-human, animals and men and the rest,

children.text: mṛtāḥ suptāśca jāgranto jñeyā [hi] maithunāśrayāḥ || Śghs_3,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: Dead, sleeping, or awake — these should be known as the bases for sexual misconduct. (3.3.2)
Beginning with a female elephant, up to a hen,

children.text: kṣudrikāṃ mahatīṃ gacchan[sa yatiś] cyavate vratāt || Śghs_3,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: One who has intercourse with a small or large [creature] — that <s>yati</s> (renunciant) falls from his vow. (3.3.3)

body.translated_text: Offenses:

children.text: raktaḥ san na striyaṃ paśyet śabdamākarṇayenna ca |
children.translated_text: One affected by passion should not look at a woman, nor listen to her voice;

children.text: nirvastraḥ san na copeyādaṃgajāta na nirbhujet || Śghs_3,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: Nor should one approach [her] unclothed, nor expose the sexual organ. (3.3.4)
A cavity made between two walls, whether dry or moist, when joined together —
One is to be expelled for the transgression when there is contact, but not otherwise. (3.3.5)

children.text: adha ūrdhvaṃ trikhaṇḍāyā vinīlādhmātikāṃ ca na |
children.translated_text: Below, above, [or in] a three-sectioned [corpse], one should not approach one that is discolored and bloated,

children.text: na cāsthisaṃkalāṃ yāyāt nābhyaktāṃ rudhirādibhiḥ || Śghs_3,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Nor one reduced to a skeleton, nor one smeared with blood and the like. (3.3.6)
A white skeleton, [or images] made of stone, wood, or clay — the <s>yati</s> (renunciant)

children.text: na ca gacchet striyaṃ yo 'tra virato maithunātsadā || Śghs_3,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: Should not approach; one who is restrained from sexual intercourse must always [avoid] a woman. (3.3.7)
One absorbed in meditation, drowsy, intoxicated, overcome by sleep,
Distracted, or afflicted by pain — if one seizes [such a person] and sits down upon them, (3.3.8)
If one relishes [the act] at the beginning, middle, or end, upon emerging from meditation,

children.text: vihārād ghaṭṭanīyaḥ so 'bhāve tu svādanasya na || Śghs_3,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: He should be removed from the <s>vihāra</s> (monastery); but if there is no relishing, then not. (3.3.9)
Relishing is like the enjoyment of rice with various condiments and sauces,
And like the drinking of oil, vinegar, <s>śauṇḍā</s> (fermented drink), and <s>āsava</s> (liquor). (3.3.10)
Non-relishing should be understood as like [the contact of] a dead dog with the neck of a youth,
Or like the touch of heated iron upon a tender person. (3.3.11)

body.translated_text: Through ignorance, such as [taking what is] not purchased, etc.,
The <s>yati</s> (renunciant) is not liable for an offense if his mind is deranged or distracted. (3.3.12)

children.translated_text: Through contact with a passionate non-human being, if the sexual organ becomes erect,

children.text: na spṛśet śukramokṣārthaṃ sa pṛthivyādidhātubhiḥ || Śghs_3,3.13 ||
children.translated_text: One should not touch it for the purpose of seminal discharge, [not even] with earth or other elements. (3.3.13)
If seminal emission occurs through contact with an animal while heedless,

children.text: [sva]mānasaṃ yatigarhet kṛtaṃ me nu virūpakaṃ || Śghs_3,3.14 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should reproach his own mind: 'An unseemly thing has been done by me.' (3.3.14)
For a <s>yati</s> (renunciant) in whom seminal discharge occurs during dreams,
In the release of semen during a dream, there is not the slightest fault. (3.3.15)

children.text: rāgāviṣṭena cittena nārīṃ na śrīghanaḥ spṛśet |
children.translated_text: With a mind seized by passion, a <s>śrīghana</s> (Jain monk) should not touch a woman;
Nor should he touch another of such nature, whether male or <s>napuṃsaka</s> (eunuch). (3.3.16)
The breasts, armpits, lips, navel, thighs, sides, belly, and private parts [of women] —

children.text: saṃraktaḥ [san] yatiḥ strīṇāṃ na nindet na ca saṃstuyāt || Śghs_3,3.17 ||
children.translated_text: An impassioned <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should neither disparage nor praise women. (3.3.17)

children.text: yadyad vadet striyaṃ[tāvat] kartukāmo yathā yathā |
children.translated_text: Whatever he would say to a woman, with whatever intention,

children.text: tattat tathā tathā brūyāt śrīghano nāntike striyāḥ || Śghs_3,3.18 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>śrīghana</s> (Jain monk) should not speak thus in the presence of a woman. (3.3.18)

children.text: agrā bhavati sā yoṣid yā māṃ paricared rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That woman is excellent who would attend to me in private,
She would be a gainer of longevity and such things, free from disease, and glorious' — (3.3.19)
Such words and the like should not be spoken by one whose mind is inflamed by the fire of passion,
By a <s>śrīghana</s> (Jain monk) in the presence of women, or of men and eunuchs likewise. (3.3.20)
A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice monk) should not act as a go-between for marriages or unions;
Nor should he perform any such errand for that purpose either. (3.3.21)
'I would give this faithful girl to him as a bride' —
It is not fitting [for a monk] to utter words that serve as a thread connecting [such] matters. (3.3.22)
One under vows should not give cows and the like for the purpose of breeding;
Nor should he ever request these from others either. (3.3.23)

children.text: tulyametāsu tvaṃ tiṣṭha mā striyā caikayā vasa |
children.translated_text: 'Remain impartially among these [wives]; do not dwell with only one woman' —

children.text: ityevaṃ hi bahustrīkaṃ puruṣaṃ na yatirvadet || Śghs_3,3.24 ||
children.translated_text: Thus a <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should not address a man who has many wives. (3.3.24)

body.translated_text: 4. The training rule on abstinence from false speech

children.translated_text: The knowledge and insight of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one), a <s>Saṃbuddha</s> (fully awakened one), and their disciples —
One who falsely claims 'I possess this' is to be expelled, unless it is from mere conceit. (3.4.1)
Knowledge is true awakening; the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) are insight;
He is not capable of claiming the knowledges such as <s>dharmānvaya</s> (inference of doctrine) and the rest. (3.4.2)
Through the speech, writing, or sign language of <s>Āryas</s> (nobles) and <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians),
If one claims knowledge and the like, it should be understood that this too is falsehood. (3.4.3)
'I dwell alone at the foot of a tree; I delight in the household;

children.text: samāhitaṃ ca me cittaṃ na ca vācyamatīndriyaṃ || Śghs_3,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: My mind is concentrated; and the super-sensory cannot be expressed in words' — (3.4.4)
One should speak of the virtues of the <s>Buddhas</s> and others, but never of oneself;

children.text: parakīyaṃ guṇaṃ pṛṣṭo brūyāttatsaṃmukhaṃ na tu || Śghs_3,4.5 ||
children.translated_text: When asked about the qualities of another, one should speak [of them], but not in that person's presence. (3.4.5)

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mataṃ yadyad vijñātaṃ caiva tad vadet |
children.translated_text: Whatever is seen, heard, thought, or cognized — that one should declare;
A <s>śrīghana</s> (Jain monk) who speaks contrarily is a speaker of falsehood. (3.4.6)
The object, the false perception, the mind so disposed,
And the false awareness with which one utters speech — one possessing [all] five factors is a speaker of untruth. (3.4.7)
One who speaks falsehood here possessing four, three, two, or one of the factors —
That <s>śrīghana</s> (Jain monk) should be known by other <s>yatis</s> (renunciants) as a speaker of falsehood. (3.4.8)
A <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should not accuse [another] face to face with a groundless, baseless [charge] such as killing a living being,

children.text: dhvaṃsanacyāvanākūtaḥ saṃmukhaṃ na ca codayet || Śghs_3,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: With the intention of destroying, causing to fall, or [exposing] a secret. (3.4.9)
For the sake of a minor offense, or even on a slight pretext,

children.text: śrāmaṇero[hi] pratyakṣaṃ [śrīghanān] na kṣipet parān || Śghs_3,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (novice monk) should not directly revile other <s>śrīghanas</s> (Jain monks). (3.4.10)
By [taunts about] birth, appearance, conduct, or speech — whether low, middling, or high — one under vows

children.text: jihmaniṣpratibhānārthaṃ na prāṇān jātu codayet || Śghs_3,4.11 ||
children.translated_text: Should never incite living beings for the purpose of rendering [them] crooked or speechless. (3.4.11)
With secondary defilements, abusive words, reproaches, offenses, and the like, a vow-keeper
Should never address a <s>yati</s> (renunciant) with the aforementioned intention. (3.4.12)

children.text: bhedaṃ yāsyati so 'nyena saṃdhāsyati mayā saha |
children.translated_text: 'He will break with another; he will make an alliance with me' —

children.text: yatira jātyādivādena paiśunyaṃ na samācaret || Śghs_3,4.13 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should not engage in <s>paiśunya</s> (slander) by speaking of [another's] caste and the like. (3.4.13)

body.translated_text: 5. The training rule on abstinence from drinking liquor, spirits, and intoxicants

children.text: madyaṃ surā ca maireyaṃ pramādasyāspadaṃ yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since <s>madya</s> (intoxicants), <s>surā</s> (liquor), and <s>maireya</s> (fermented drink) are the basis of heedlessness,

children.text: na parasmai[hi] taddeyaṃ na ca peyaṃ śvamūtravata || Śghs_3,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: These should neither be given to another nor drunk — [they are] like dog's urine. (3.5.1)
One [type of <s>surā</s>] is made with bark and jaggery, another with [bark] alone,
And <s>surā</s> (liquor) is also prepared with flour, yeast, and water. (3.5.2)
<s>Maireya</s> (fermented drink) is that which is prepared with jaggery, <s>dhātrī</s> (emblic myrobalan), water, and <s>dhātakī</s> (Woodfordia fruticosa);

children.text: kuśāgreṇāpi tat pātuṃ yatīnāṃ na prakalpate || Śghs_3,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: Even with [a drop on] the tip of a blade of <s>kuśa</s> grass, it is not permissible for <s>yatis</s> (renunciants) to drink it. (3.5.3)

body.text: kodravānnaṃ na bhuñjīta tatpalāle ca na svapet ||
body.translated_text: One should not eat food made from <s>kodrava</s> (millet), nor sleep on its straw;

body.text: pītaṃ sata madayed yacca pātavyaṃ tadapīha na || Śghs_3,5.4 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever, when drunk, would intoxicate — that too should not be drunk here. (3.5.4)
6. The training rule on abstinence from high beds and large beds

children.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should sit on a bed whose legs are [no more than] eight finger-breadths according to the <s>Jina</s>'s [rule],

children.text: [vinā] śalyena[maṃce vā] hemarūpyakṛte na tu || Śghs_3,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: Or on a cot without [sharp] points, but not one made of gold or silver. (3.6.1)

children.text: sāṃghike śayane dadyāt tat pratyāstaraṇaṃ yatiḥ |
children.translated_text: On a communal bed, the <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should place a covering;
For cloth and blanket, the prescribed [thickness] is three-fold, two-fold, and single-fold respectively. (3.6.2)
Having placed the legs [of the cot] in pits, [the legs being] of no more than the proper measure,

children.text: prakṣipya pratipādeṣu ṭaṃkitvā kīlakeṣu vā || Śghs_3,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: Inserting [them] into the supports or fastening [them] with pegs — (3.6.3)
In this way, the <s>yati</s> (renunciant) should sleep on a cot for protection from mice, ants, and the like;
He should not let his feet hang down [from] a long-legged [bed] while traveling. (3.6.4)

body.text: alpaṃ ced dvādaśebhyo hi deyamekaṃ vihārakaṃ |

children.text: nirmuṣṭahastaṃ svalpatve bahutve tu viparyayāt | Śghs_3,6.5 ||
children.translated_text: [Measuring] the span of a fist-less hand; when few [it is thus], but when many, the reverse. (3.6.5)

body.translated_text: If [the monks] are few, for twelve [monks] one <s>vihāra</s> (dwelling) should be given,

children.text: stokaṃ ced navakaḥ pīṭhe vṛddho maṃce[tadā] svapet |
children.translated_text: If [the monks are] few, a junior should sleep on a stool and an elder on a cot;
A junior may also sleep at the foot of a tree, in the open air. (3.6.6)
During the rainy season, another fellow monk should not be installed
[In] one's own <s>vihāra</s> (dwelling); rather, the <s>yati</s> (renunciant) [should be accommodated] according to seniority. (3.6.7)
For the purpose of ritual preparation and use, and for the purpose of maintenance,
The communal bedding and seating is designated [for the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.6.8 //
Three types of lodging — inferior, middling, and superior — [should be established for the <s>bhikṣus</s>];
For the elderly and other visitors, one should assign [these] in descending order [of seniority]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.6.9 //
An excessively high bed or seat is prohibited for a <s>yati</s> (renunciant), because
It causes pride and haughtiness, and is a reason for the contempt of worldly people. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.6.10 //

body.translated_text: 7. The training rule on abstention from dancing, singing, and music.

children.translated_text: Dancing involving the throwing about of arms, singing in a loud voice,
And playing instruments such as the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute), flute, and <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drum) — one should not play [these]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.7.1 //

body.translated_text: 8. The training rule on abstention from perfumes, garlands, and cosmetics.

children.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> (renunciant) may wear perfumes such as sandalwood [only when] ill,
Having first offered [some] to a <s>muni</s> (sage), and on the instruction of a physician. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.1 //

children.text: na tiṣṭhet prakaṭe deśe kṣālayitvā bahirvrajet |
children.translated_text: One should not stand in a public place; having washed [it off], one should go outside.
By this very procedure, one should wear flower garlands [when ill]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.2 //
For one suffering from eye disease, headache, <s>pūtanā</s> (fever), or planet-seizure illness,

children.text: mālayā veṣṭayet śīrṣaṃ mekhalāṃ na ca laṃbayet || Śghs_3,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: One may wrap the head with a garland, but should not hang down a girdle. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.3 //
With powder of orpiment and similar substances, or with fragrant oil,

children.text: na vadanādikaṃ gātraṃ varṇārthaṃ marṣayed yatiḥ || Śghs_3,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> should not anoint the face or other body parts for the purpose of beautification. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.4 //
Because perfumes, garlands, and cosmetics are unbefitting for a <s>yati</s>,

children.text: rāgauddhatyakaraṃ yasmāt tasmāttad garhitaṃ jinaiḥ || Śghs_3,8.5 ||
children.translated_text: And because they produce attachment and haughtiness — therefore they are censured by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones). // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.5 //

children.text: na darpaṇe nirīkṣeta mukhaṃ vā tailabhājane |
children.translated_text: One should not look at one's face in a mirror or in an oil vessel,
Unless one is suffering from head pain or eye disease requiring examination. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.6 //
One should not anoint one's own face with oil for the purpose of adornment;
Nor should there be anointing [even] for cracked lips, facial or head ailments, without [medical] reason. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.7 //
A <s>yati</s> should not decorate the face with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) powder and similar substances;
However, a paste of sesame and similar substances is permitted for the relief of pimples. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.8.8 //

body.translated_text: 9. The training rule on abstention from eating at the wrong time.

children.translated_text: 'When I ate at night in other [times], a slight illness occurred in me.'
'Likewise indeed should you do — [food] should be eaten only during the day.' // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.1 //
Falling into a pit of excrement and urine, encounters with thieves and serpents —
People will think disparagingly, 'They wander about in houses for the sake of their bellies.' // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.2 //
Those who wander for alms in the evening and morning, and eat [at those times],
In assemblies, courtyards, crossroads, temples, and houses — // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.3 //

body.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s> (the Well-Gone One, i.e., the <s>Buddha</s>) said: a <s>yati</s> should eat at the [proper] time;
After sunrise up to noon, [but] not beyond the measure of a hair's [shadow past noon]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.4 //

children.translated_text: Barley meal, cooked rice, porridge of pulses, fish, and meat are time-restricted foods;
Lifelong [intake of] oil and similar [substances], and drinking of long pepper should be avoided. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.5 //
Whatever is eaten with the teeth or introduced into the throat,
And whatever fills the stomach — one should eat that at the time as prescribed. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.6 //
Barley meal and other [foods] free from meat, waterless [i.e., solid], such as clay-water and similar,
And hailstones — a <s>yati</s> afflicted by thirst may eat ice. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.7 //
In the place where allowable water is [stored], the two hands should not be washed [if stained with blood];

children.text: hastau dvau cāṃgulīkṣāle na grāhyaṃ kalpikodakaṃ || Śghs_3,9.8 ||
children.translated_text: Nor should allowable water be taken with two hands or with finger-washing. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.8 //

children.text: māyāśāṭhaya[yutaḥ] kuryāt na ca prakṣālanaṃ tayoḥ |
children.translated_text: One should not wash them [the hands] with deceit and cunning;

children.text: saśabdau [yadi] tau śuddhau vedyau snigdhatvaco yateḥ || Śghs_3,9.9 ||
children.translated_text: If both [hands] make a sound [i.e., are clean], the skin of the <s>yati</s> should be known as smooth [clean]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.9 //
'Will you not give me food to eat? Tormented by hunger and thirst, [I shall die]!'

children.text: ityevaṃ [sa] viruktaḥ syāt kṣeptavyo maṇḍakuṇḍa[ke] || Śghs_3,9.10 ||
children.translated_text: One who cries out thus in distress should be thrown out of the assembly. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.10 //
In the eight [permitted ways], washed grain placed in a non-meat vessel,

children.text: sphuṭaṃ tu yadi pātuṃ tannaiva glānāya kalpate || Śghs_3,9.11 ||
children.translated_text: If clearly [prepared] — but if [meant] for drinking, that is not suitable for the sick. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.11 //
That which is acquired through greed by corrupted speech, body, and action —
Dwelling, robes, and food — one should avoid like poisoned food. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.12 //
One who has taken the vow should not engage in, cause to be done, or arrange livelihood through

children.text: na kārayet na kuryānna jīvikāṃ tena kalpayet || Śghs_3,9.13 ||
children.translated_text: The selling of liquor, weapons, poison, living beings, or lac. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.13 //
<s>Kuhanā</s> (hypocrisy) is the restraint of the senses for the purpose of gaining respect and profit;
<s>Lapanā</s> (flattery) is speaking sweet words for the purpose of obtaining robes and similar [items]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.14 //
<s>Naiṣpeṣikatva</s> (insinuation) is disparaging others for the sake of obtaining food and similar [items];
<s>Naimittikatva</s> (hinting) is the description of another's bowl and similar [possessions]. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.15 //
Seeking profit through [previous] gains, and seeking increase of gains —
A <s>yati</s> should avoid these wrong livelihoods like excrement. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.16 //
Play, harming others, and contemptible [conduct] of body and speech always —
One who has taken the vow should constantly avoid [these] like a snake smeared with excrement. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.17 //
In a market, tavern, thicket, gambling house, or prison —
These are declared out of bounds; a <s>celaka</s> (novice) should not remain there. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.9.18 //

body.translated_text: 10. The training rule on abstention from accepting gold and silver.

children.translated_text: With the body, with hands and feet, with robes, umbrella, and similar [items], the one with the vow

children.text: rajataṃ jātarūpaṃ ca na spṛśet jvalitāgnivat || Śghs_3,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: Should not touch silver or gold, as [one would not touch] a blazing fire. // <s>Śghs</s> 3.10.1 //

body.text: iti saṃghasenena saṃvihitoddhāre śrīghanācārasaṃgrahe śrāmaṇerabhāvopāyo nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāya ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, named 'The Means to the <s>Śrāmaṇera</s> (Novice) State,' in the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> restored by <s>Saṃghasena</s>.
Chapter Four: Other Observances.

children.translated_text: A <s>yati</s> who [is busy with] <s>campū</s> (gargling), quarrels, tooth-sticks, attending the elderly,
Bathing, drinking, eating, reciting hymns, [or who is] busy, naked, or wearing a single garment — // <s>Śghs</s> 4.1 //
One occupied with pottery work, going quickly to a two- or three-storied [building],

children.text: āśu vrajan pacan pātraṃ vyagraś cīvarakarmaṇā || Śghs_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: Walking hurriedly, cooking, [holding] a bowl, or busy with robe-making — // <s>Śghs</s> 4.2 //
One engaged in grinding cloth, with painted eyes, or drinking gray [liquid],

children.text: likhan yo pustakaṃ vāpi yo vācayati so 'pi na || Śghs_4.3 ||
children.translated_text: One who is writing a book, or one who is teaching — he too [is not to be saluted]. // <s>Śghs</s> 4.3 //
One going to the latrine, standing in darkness, or urinating,

children.text: vāsayannatha prāvṛṇvana na vandyo yatinā yatiḥ || Śghs_4.4 ||
children.translated_text: Or one who is dressing or undressing — a <s>yati</s> should not salute [such] a <s>yati</s>. // <s>Śghs</s> 4.4 //
With head covered, or [standing] on a stairway, or on the knees,

children.text: muṇḍasphoṭaṃ hi jaṃghāyāṃ na dadyādavinā yathā || Śghs_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: One should not give a slap on the shins — as [would be done] without [proper] training. // <s>Śghs</s> 4.5 //
By one sitting at equal level, while being saluted, at [the other's] pair of feet,
Having grasped [them] with a crab-like grip, one should say 'May you be healthy!' // <s>Śghs</s> 4.6 //
Other observances have been extracted from the abridgement of the <s>Bhikṣu-vinaya</s> (monks' discipline);
The rest should be heard from the preceptor, and should be practiced with reverence. // <s>Śghs</s> 4.7 //
Having compiled the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> in two hundred [verses],

children.text: sukṛtaṃ karma yattena jano prāpnotvasaṃskṛtaṃ || Śghs_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: May people, through the merit produced thereby, attain the <s>asaṃskṛta</s> (the unconditioned, i.e., <s>Nirvāṇa</s>). // <s>Śghs</s> 4.8 //

body.text:
iti saṃghasenena saṃvihitoddhāre śrīghanācārasaṃgrahe
anye cācārā nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'Other Observances,' in the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s> restored by <s>Saṃghasena</s>.
Thus ends the <s>Śrīghanācārasaṃgraha</s>.
